name: AIM 2022 Reversed ISP and RAW Reconstruction Challenge
description: Cameras capture sensor RAW images and transform them into pleasant RGB images, suitable for the human eyes, using their integrated Image Signal Processor (ISP). Numerous low-level vision tasks operate in the RAW domain (e.g. image denoising, white balance) due to its linear relationship with the scene irradiance, wide-range of information at 12bits, and sensor designs. Despite this, RAW image datasets are scarce and more expensive to collect than the already large and public RGB datasets. This paper introduces the AIM 2022 Challenge on Reversed Image Signal Processing and RAW Reconstruction. We aim to recover raw sensor images from the corresponding RGBs without metadata and, by doing this, "reverse" the ISP transformation. The proposed methods and benchmark establish the state-of-the-art for this low-level vision inverse problem, and generating realistic raw sensor readings can potentially benefit other tasks such as denoising and super-resolution.
evaluation_method: PSNR and SSIM (primary), sometimes perceptual metrics and downstream task performance
general_score_metric: peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), often reported alongside SSIM
reputation: Recognized within the computational-photography and low-level vision community as a focused challenge for RAW reconstruction; moderate adoption among researchers in the subfield.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; dataset size and camera-specific ISP mappings can limit generalization; lacking metadata increases realism of the reverse-ISP problem but also ambiguity; standard pixel metrics (PSNR/SSIM) may not fully reflect perceptual quality.
